note: Curated situation lines and background stories for the Hadith Library. overlays attach to verified entries in AI Model/hadith-500-tasalli.json by sunnah.com key; additions are English meanings pending verbatim text + Arabic from sunnah.com and scholar review.

muslim:2999.situation: When everything feels like it is going wrong

bukhari:5641.situation: When you feel your pain is meaningless

bukhari:6369.situation: When anxiety will not leave you
bukhari:6369.story: Anas served the Prophet ﷺ for years and said he heard him repeat this supplication many times, which shows that even the best of people sought Allah's protection from worry.

bukhari:6346.situation: When you feel trapped and need relief

tirmidhi:2516.situation: When you feel alone against the world
tirmidhi:2516.story: Ibn Abbas was only a boy riding behind the Prophet ﷺ on a mount when he was told, “Young man, I will teach you some words.” These words became one of the most loved reminders of trust in Allah.

muslim:2664.situation: When you keep thinking 'if only I had…'

bukhari:1303.situation: When you feel guilty for crying
bukhari:1303.story: The Prophet ﷺ held his infant son Ibrahim as he passed away, and tears ran from his eyes. A companion was surprised to see him weep, and he explained that tears are a mercy, as long as the tongue stays content with Allah.

bukhari:1283.story: The Prophet ﷺ passed a woman weeping at a grave and told her to fear Allah and be patient. Not recognising him, she said, 'Leave me, you have not been struck as I have.' Later she learned who he was and came to apologise. He gently taught her that patience counts most in the first moment of shock.

bukhari:6424.situation: When you feel your loss will go unrewarded

bukhari:1284.situation: When you watch a loved one suffering
bukhari:1284.story: The Prophet's daughter Zaynab sent for him as her little son was dying. He came, held the child, and his eyes overflowed. When Sa'd asked about the tears, he answered with these words.

bukhari:1469.situation: When you are running out of patience
bukhari:1469.story: Some people of the Ansar asked the Prophet ﷺ for help again and again until what he had ran out. He then reminded them that self-restraint, contentment and patience are themselves gifts from Allah.

bukhari:5652.situation: When you live with a long-term condition
bukhari:5652.story: A Black woman of Madinah who suffered from epilepsy came to the Prophet ﷺ. She chose patience and Paradise, asking only for her dignity to be protected. Ibn Abbas would point her out and say, 'Shall I show you a woman of Paradise?'

bukhari:5671.situation: When you are tempted to wish your life away

ibnmajah:4032.situation: When others hurt you and you hold back

bukhari:2996.situation: When you cannot do your usual worship because you are ill

bukhari:5678.situation: When you are searching for a cure

muslim:2202.situation: When you are in physical pain
muslim:2202.story: Uthman ibn Abi al-As complained to the Prophet ﷺ of a pain he had felt in his body since becoming Muslim. He taught him this practice, and Uthman later said Allah removed the pain.

muslim:2575.situation: When a fever wears you down
muslim:2575.story: The Prophet ﷺ visited Umm as-Sa'ib, who was shivering with fever. When she cursed the fever, he gently corrected her with these words.

bukhari:6114.situation: When you think strength means winning the argument

bukhari:3282.situation: In the middle of a heated fight
bukhari:3282.story: Two men were insulting each other in front of the Prophet ﷺ, and one became red-faced with rage, his veins swelling. The Prophet ﷺ said this sentence, teaching that anger is often a whisper to be pushed away.

abudawud:4782.situation: When anger takes over your body

abudawud:4811.situation: When you forget to thank the people around you

tirmidhi:2346.situation: When you feel you have nothing

bukhari:6446.situation: When you want more and more

abudawud:4985.situation: When you need rest for your heart
abudawud:4985.story: For the Prophet ﷺ, prayer was not a chore to get through but the place where he found rest and comfort after a long day.

muslim:482.situation: When you want to feel close to Allah

bukhari:1145.situation: When you cannot sleep at night

abudawud:1488.situation: When you feel too unworthy to raise your hands

bukhari:7405.situation: When you feel far from Allah

bukhari:6306.situation: Morning and evening, to seek forgiveness

bukhari:5010.situation: Before you sleep, when you feel unsafe
bukhari:5010.story: Abu Hurayrah was guarding the zakah food when a man came three nights in a row to steal from it. Each time he begged to be let go. On the third night he taught Abu Hurayrah this verse in exchange. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'He told you the truth, though he is a liar. That was Shaytan.'

bukhari:5971.situation: When you wonder who deserves your care most

bukhari:3004.situation: When you are torn between your goals and your parents

tirmidhi:1899.situation: When pleasing your parents feels hard

bukhari:2620.situation: When your parent does not share your faith
bukhari:2620.story: Asma's mother, who was not Muslim, came to visit her hoping for kindness. Asma asked the Prophet ﷺ whether she should keep ties with her, and he told her to be good to her mother.

bukhari:5986.situation: When you want blessing in your life

bukhari:5991.situation: When relatives do not return your kindness

bukhari:6077.situation: When you have stopped talking to someone

bukhari:56.situation: When you feel spending on your family is 'just bills'

tirmidhi:3895.situation: When you want to be a better spouse

bukhari:676.situation: When housework becomes a point of tension

bukhari:5090.situation: When you are choosing a spouse

bukhari:5997.situation: When you hold back affection from your children
bukhari:5997.story: The Prophet ﷺ kissed his grandson Hasan. Al-Aqra' ibn Habis, sitting nearby, said, 'I have ten children and I have never kissed any of them.' The Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said these words.

muslim:1631.situation: When you wonder what you will leave behind

tirmidhi:1956.situation: When you have nothing material to give

bukhari:13.situation: When you feel jealous of someone's success

bukhari:6094.situation: When a lie would make things easier

muslim:2589.situation: When the conversation turns to gossip

bukhari:2072.situation: When you feel your job is beneath you

tirmidhi:3540.situation: When your sins feel as high as the sky

bukhari:6307.situation: When you think seeking forgiveness is only for sinners

muslim:2749.situation: When you feel like a failure

tirmidhi:1987.situation: When you want to make up for a wrong

bukhari:6000.situation: When you need to remember how merciful Allah is

bukhari:1.story: Scholars mention that a man emigrated to Madinah not for the faith but to marry a woman called Umm Qays. The hadith teaches that the same outward action can carry very different worth depending on the heart behind it.

bukhari:6491.situation: When you meant to do good but could not

bukhari:6117.situation: When you feel shy or modest

muslim:2626.situation: When you think a small good deed is worthless

muslim:2588.situation: When you feel humble acts lower you

bukhari:6065.situation: When envy or resentment creeps in

bukhari:5027.situation: When you are learning or teaching the Qur'an

bukhari:4937.situation: When you stumble while reading the Qur'an

bukhari:1417.situation: When you have very little to give

bukhari:6416.situation: When this world feels too heavy
bukhari:6416.story: The Prophet ﷺ took Ibn Umar by the shoulder and said these words. Ibn Umar would add: 'In the evening, do not wait for the morning; in the morning, do not wait for the evening. Take from your health for your sickness and from your life for your death.'

additions.text: The supplication of Dhun-Nun (Prophet Yunus) when he was in the belly of the whale was: “There is no god but You, glory be to You; truly I was among the wrongdoers.” No Muslim calls upon Allah with it for anything except that Allah answers him.
additions.situation: When you are in the 'belly of the whale' moment
additions.story: Yunus (peace be upon him) left his people in frustration and was swallowed by a great fish. In darkness upon darkness he did not complain; he praised Allah and admitted his own fault, and Allah rescued him. The Prophet ﷺ taught that this same dua is a key for anyone in distress.

additions.text: The greatness of the reward comes with the greatness of the trial. When Allah loves a people He tests them. Whoever is content will have contentment, and whoever is resentful will have resentment.
additions.situation: When you wonder why you are being tested

additions.text: Look at those who are below you and do not look at those who are above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the blessings Allah has given you.
additions.situation: When you compare your life with others

additions.topic: Grief, loss & death of loved ones
additions.text: There is no Muslim struck by a calamity who says what Allah has commanded, “To Allah we belong and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better,” except that Allah replaces it for him with something better.
additions.situation: When you have lost someone dear
additions.story: When her husband Abu Salamah died, Umm Salamah said this dua while thinking, 'Who could be better than Abu Salamah?' Allah then replaced him with someone better: she married the Prophet ﷺ himself.

additions.topic: Grief, loss & death of loved ones
additions.text: Any woman among you who loses three of her children, they will be a shield for her from the Fire. A woman asked, 'And two?' He said, 'And two.'
additions.situation: When a parent has lost a child
additions.story: The women of Madinah asked the Prophet ﷺ to set aside a day to teach them, since the men took up his time. On that day he gave them this comfort for mothers who had buried their children.

additions.topic: Grief, loss & death of loved ones
additions.text: When a servant's child dies, Allah asks the angels, 'You have taken the fruit of his heart?' They say yes. He asks, 'What did My servant say?' They say, 'He praised You and said: To Allah we belong and to Him we return.' Allah says, 'Build for My servant a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.'
additions.situation: When your child has passed away

additions.text: When the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick person he would say: “La ba's, tahurun in sha Allah” — No harm, it is a purification, if Allah wills.
additions.situation: When you visit someone who is sick
additions.story: He visited a Bedouin with a fever and said these words of comfort. The man answered bitterly that it was a fever boiling in an old man that would take him to the grave. The Prophet ﷺ replied, 'Then so be it,' showing that comfort is offered but the heart must accept it.

additions.text: If you hear of a plague in a land, do not enter it; and if it breaks out in a land where you are, do not leave it.
additions.situation: When there is an outbreak or epidemic
additions.story: Umar ibn al-Khattab was travelling to Syria when news arrived of a plague there. After consulting the companions, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf reported this hadith, and Umar turned back, saying they were fleeing from one decree of Allah to another decree of Allah.

additions.text: Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me.' He will say, 'How could I visit You when You are the Lord of the worlds?' Allah will say, 'Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him? Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him.'
additions.situation: When a friend or relative is in hospital

additions.text: Whoever restrains his anger while he is able to act on it, Allah will call him before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection and let him choose whichever of the maidens of Paradise he wishes.
additions.situation: When you could take revenge but choose not to

additions.text: Gently, O Aisha! Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters.
additions.situation: When someone is rude to you
additions.story: A group came to the Prophet ﷺ and, twisting the greeting, said 'Death be upon you.' Aisha answered back harshly. The Prophet ﷺ only replied 'And upon you,' and taught her that gentleness is loved by Allah even when facing rudeness.

additions.text: Gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disfigures it.
additions.situation: When you want to handle a situation well

additions.text: Should I not be a grateful servant?
additions.situation: When worship feels like a burden
additions.story: The Prophet ﷺ prayed at night until his feet cracked and swelled. Aisha asked why he did this when Allah had already forgiven him. His answer showed that worship can come from love and thankfulness, not only from fear.

additions.text: Allah is pleased with a servant who eats a meal and praises Him for it, and drinks a drink and praises Him for it.
additions.situation: At mealtimes

additions.text: Whenever something distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he would pray.
additions.situation: When something troubles you

additions.text: If there were a river at the door of one of you and he bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain on him? That is the example of the five prayers: through them Allah wipes away sins.
additions.situation: When you feel weighed down by your sins

additions.text: The first deed for which a servant will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection is his prayer. If it is sound, he will have succeeded; if it is defective, he will have failed and lost.
additions.situation: When you are struggling to pray regularly

additions.text: I asked the Prophet ﷺ which deed is most beloved to Allah. He said, 'Prayer at its proper time.' I asked, 'Then what?' He said, 'Kindness to parents.' I asked, 'Then what?' He said, 'Striving in the way of Allah.'
additions.situation: When you wonder which deeds matter most

additions.text: The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than this world and everything in it.
additions.situation: When it is hard to get up for Fajr

additions.text: Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees better than prayer offered alone.
additions.situation: When you are deciding whether to pray at the mosque

additions.text: Whoever prays the morning (Fajr) prayer is under the protection of Allah.
additions.situation: When you are afraid of the day ahead

additions.text: The supplication of any of you will be answered as long as he is not impatient and says, 'I prayed but I was not answered.'
additions.situation: When it feels like your dua is not answered

additions.text: There is no Muslim on earth who calls upon Allah with a supplication except that Allah gives him what he asked, or turns away from him an equal harm, as long as he does not ask for something sinful or for cutting family ties.
additions.situation: When you doubt that asking makes a difference

additions.topic: Remembrance of Allah & peace of heart
additions.text: The example of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not is like the example of the living and the dead.
additions.situation: When your heart feels dead

additions.topic: Remembrance of Allah & peace of heart
additions.text: Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the scales and beloved to the Most Merciful: 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil-Azim' (Glory be to Allah and praise Him; glory be to Allah the Magnificent).
additions.situation: When you want something easy to say every day

additions.topic: Remembrance of Allah & peace of heart
additions.text: Shall I not tell you of something better than a servant? When you go to bed, say SubhanAllah thirty-three times, Alhamdulillah thirty-three times and Allahu Akbar thirty-four times. That is better for you than a servant.
additions.situation: When you are exhausted by housework and responsibilities
additions.story: Fatimah's hands were blistered from grinding grain, and she went to ask her father ﷺ for a servant from the captives. He came to her and Ali at night and gave them this dhikr instead, a source of strength for every tired person since.

additions.topic: Remembrance of Allah & peace of heart
additions.text: Shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' (There is no power and no strength except with Allah).
additions.situation: When a task seems impossible

additions.text: No Muslim servant supplicates for his brother in his absence except that an angel says: 'And for you the same.'
additions.situation: When you want to help a friend who is struggling

additions.text: “Do you have a mother?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Then stay with her, for Paradise is beneath her feet.”
additions.situation: When you want to do great deeds but your mother needs you

additions.text: May his nose be rubbed in dust, may his nose be rubbed in dust! The one whose parents, one or both, reach old age while he is with them, and he does not enter Paradise (by serving them).
additions.situation: When your parents are growing old

additions.text: Three men were trapped in a cave by a rock. Each called on Allah by a sincere good deed. One said: 'O Allah, I had elderly parents and I never gave my family milk before them. One night I came late and they were asleep, so I stood holding the cup until dawn, while my children cried at my feet. If I did that for Your sake, relieve us.' And the rock moved.
additions.situation: When you think small acts of service do not count
additions.story: The Prophet ﷺ told this story of three men from a previous nation. Each was saved by one sincere deed: kindness to parents, chastity, and honesty with a worker's wages. Together the deeds opened the cave.

additions.text: Among the finest acts of goodness is that a person keeps ties with the people his father loved.
additions.situation: After your parents have passed away

additions.text: A man said, 'I have relatives: I keep ties with them and they cut me off, I treat them well and they treat me badly.' The Prophet ﷺ said, 'If you are as you say, it is as if you are feeding them hot ashes, and you will have a helper from Allah against them as long as you continue.'
additions.situation: When family members keep hurting you

additions.text: A believing man should not hate a believing woman. If he dislikes one of her traits, he will be pleased with another.
additions.situation: When your spouse annoys you

additions.text: This world is a provision, and the best provision of this world is a righteous woman.
additions.situation: When you appreciate a good partner

additions.text: Aisha said: I raced the Prophet ﷺ and beat him. Later, when I had put on weight, we raced again and he beat me, and he said, 'This makes up for that one.'
additions.situation: When marriage has become all routine and no joy
additions.story: On a journey the Prophet ﷺ sent the army ahead so he and Aisha could race. Years later he remembered the first race and teased her after winning the second, a picture of warmth and play in marriage.

additions.text: Khadijah said: 'Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep ties with your relatives, you carry the burdens of the weak, you help the poor, you honour your guests and you support people in times of hardship.'
additions.situation: When your spouse is frightened or overwhelmed
additions.story: After the first revelation in the cave of Hira, the Prophet ﷺ came home trembling and said, 'Cover me.' Khadijah did not panic or doubt him. She reminded him of his good character and took him to her cousin Waraqah. Her support is a model of how spouses steady each other.

additions.text: Whoever raises two girls until they reach adulthood, he and I will come on the Day of Resurrection like this — and he joined his fingers together.
additions.situation: When you are raising daughters

additions.text: My son was riding on my back, and I did not want to hurry him until he had finished.
additions.situation: When kids interrupt your worship
additions.story: During a prayer, the Prophet ﷺ stayed in prostration so long that the people thought something had happened. Afterwards he explained that his grandson had climbed onto his back and he did not want to rush him.

additions.text: I begin the prayer intending to make it long, then I hear a child crying and I shorten it, because I know how much the mother is troubled by his crying.
additions.situation: When a child cries during prayer

additions.text: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. The man is a shepherd over his family, and the woman is a shepherd over her husband's house and children.
additions.situation: When you feel the weight of responsibility

additions.text: Fear Allah and be fair between your children.
additions.situation: When you are tempted to favour one child
additions.story: An-Nu'man's father gave him a special gift and asked the Prophet ﷺ to witness it. The Prophet ﷺ asked, 'Did you give the same to all your children?' When he said no, the Prophet ﷺ refused to witness it, and the father took the gift back.

additions.text: Jibril kept advising me to treat the neighbour well until I thought he would make him an heir.
additions.situation: When your neighbour is difficult

additions.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his neighbour. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest.
additions.situation: When you have guests or neighbours around

additions.text: A man was walking and became very thirsty. He went down into a well and drank. When he came out he saw a dog panting and licking the mud from thirst. He went down again, filled his shoe with water and gave the dog a drink. Allah appreciated this and forgave him. The companions asked, 'Is there reward for us in animals?' He said, 'In every living creature there is reward.'
additions.situation: When you think kindness to animals is small

additions.text: A woman was punished because of a cat she locked up until it died. She neither fed it nor let it go to eat from the creatures of the earth.
additions.situation: When you are careless with animals

additions.text: The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will be merciful to you.
additions.situation: When you need Allah's mercy

additions.text: Every joint of a person must give charity every day the sun rises: judging fairly between two people is charity, helping a man onto his mount is charity, a good word is charity, every step to the prayer is charity, and removing something harmful from the road is charity.
additions.situation: When you think you cannot do much good

additions.text: Whoever relieves a believer of a hardship of this world, Allah will relieve him of a hardship of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things easy for someone in difficulty, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the next. Allah helps His servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
additions.situation: When a friend is going through a hard time

additions.text: The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays.
additions.situation: When you are tempted to break a promise

additions.text: A servant may speak a word without thinking about it, and because of it he slips into the Fire farther than the distance between east and west.
additions.situation: Before you post or say something carelessly

additions.text: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt. Truthfulness brings peace of mind, and lying brings doubt.
additions.situation: When you are unsure whether something is right

additions.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
additions.situation: When you want to know who a true Muslim is

additions.text: Ka'b said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah saved me only because of my truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will speak nothing but the truth for as long as I live.'
additions.situation: When telling the truth may cost you
additions.story: Ka'b stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk without an excuse. Others made up excuses; Ka'b told the plain truth. He was boycotted for fifty days until the earth felt narrow for him. Then Allah revealed verses accepting his repentance. He said his honesty was the reason he was saved.

additions.text: If you relied on Allah as He truly should be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening.
additions.situation: When you are anxious about money

additions.text: A man asked, 'Should I tie my camel and trust in Allah, or leave it untied and trust in Allah?' He said, 'Tie it and trust in Allah.'
additions.situation: When you wonder if trusting Allah means not planning

additions.text: For one of you to take a rope, gather a bundle of firewood on his back and sell it, so that Allah protects his dignity by it, is better than asking people, whether they give him or refuse him.
additions.situation: When you are tempted to rely on others

additions.text: The upper hand is better than the lower hand. The upper hand is the one that gives, and the lower hand is the one that asks.
additions.situation: When you are building your independence

additions.text: The buyer and the seller have the option to cancel as long as they have not parted. If they were honest and made everything clear, their deal will be blessed. If they concealed and lied, the blessing of their deal will be wiped out.
additions.situation: When you run a business

additions.text: Whoever cheats is not one of us.
additions.situation: When you are tempted to hide a product's flaw
additions.story: In the market the Prophet ﷺ put his hand into a pile of grain and found it wet underneath. The seller said rain had fallen on it. He said, 'Why not put the wet part on top so people can see it?' and then said these words.

additions.text: Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.
additions.situation: When you employ or pay someone

additions.text: Allah is more delighted with the repentance of His servant than one of you who was on his camel in a barren desert. It ran away carrying his food and drink, and he lost all hope and lay down in the shade of a tree. Then suddenly there it was, standing beside him. He grabbed its rope and, out of extreme joy, said: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your Lord!' — he made a mistake out of extreme joy.
additions.situation: When you think Allah will not forgive you

additions.text: A man had killed ninety-nine people. He asked a monk if he could repent, and the monk said no, so he killed him too. Then a scholar told him, 'Who can stand between you and repentance? Go to such-and-such a land where people worship Allah.' He set out and died on the way. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. They measured the distance and found him closer to the land he was heading toward, so the angels of mercy took him.
additions.situation: When you feel it is too late for you
additions.story: In one narration Allah commanded the land he left to move farther away and the land he sought to come closer. What mattered was that he had turned around and started walking.

additions.text: Every child of Adam makes mistakes, and the best of those who make mistakes are those who repent.
additions.situation: When you keep making the same mistake

additions.text: Allah stretches out His hand at night so that the one who sinned during the day may repent, and He stretches out His hand during the day so that the one who sinned at night may repent, until the sun rises from the west.
additions.situation: After a bad day

additions.text: “Do you think this woman would throw her child into the fire?” We said, “No, by Allah.” He said, “Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child.”
additions.situation: When you doubt Allah loves you
additions.story: Captives were brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and a woman among them was frantically searching for her baby. When she found him she pulled him close and nursed him. The Prophet ﷺ pointed to her and used her love to show the companions the far greater mercy of Allah.

additions.text: Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearance, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
additions.situation: When you feel judged by appearances

additions.text: Nothing will be heavier on the scale of the believer on the Day of Resurrection than good character.
additions.situation: When you want the heaviest deed on your scale

additions.text: I was sent only to perfect good character.
additions.situation: When you want to understand the Prophet's mission

additions.text: No one who has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise. A man said, 'A person likes his clothes and shoes to be nice.' He said, 'Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.'
additions.situation: When you feel proud or superior

additions.text: When Allah wants good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion.
additions.situation: When you want Allah to want good for you

additions.text: Read the Qur'an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companions.
additions.situation: When you need a reason to open the Qur'an today

additions.text: Among the seven whom Allah will shade on the Day when there is no shade but His: a man who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives, and a man who remembers Allah in private and his eyes overflow with tears.
additions.situation: When you want your giving to stay private

additions.text: Every act of goodness is charity.
additions.situation: When you wonder what counts as charity

additions.text: A prostitute saw a dog circling a well on a hot day, its tongue hanging out from thirst. She drew water for it with her shoe, and she was forgiven because of it.
additions.situation: When you think your past rules out good deeds

additions.text: None of you should die except while thinking well of Allah.
additions.situation: When you are afraid of meeting Allah

additions.text: Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has ever imagined.
additions.situation: When you dream of something better than this life

additions.text: The person who suffered the most hardship in this world, from the people of Paradise, will be dipped once into Paradise and asked, 'O son of Adam, did you ever see any hardship? Did you ever go through any difficulty?' He will say, 'No, by Allah, my Lord. I never saw any hardship and never went through any difficulty.'
additions.situation: When your whole life has felt like suffering

additions.text: Whoever's last words are 'La ilaha illallah' (there is no god but Allah) will enter Paradise.
additions.situation: When you sit with someone who is dying

additions.text: Remember often the destroyer of pleasures: death.
additions.situation: When you get too attached to pleasures

additions.text: When Allah completed creation, He wrote in a Book that is with Him above the Throne: 'My mercy prevails over My anger.'
additions.situation: When you need hope that mercy wins in the end
